input: Research Carvana (carvana.com) for a hedge fund

risks.claim: Funding-model concentration: loan origination/monetization generated ~$1.2B profit in 2025 (56% of EBITDA); a freeze in securitization markets or reduced buyer appetite would create material liquidity needs given ~$13B of 2025 originations; 2022-2023 ABS vintages are already performing worse than S&P's expectations

Per-unit profitability is eroding: total GPU $6,997 (-$365 YoY), other GPU -$307 on more competitive financing, Adjusted EBITDA margin 10.0% vs 11.3% a year ago, and Adjusted EBITDA per retail unit fell to ~$3,680 from ~$4,085

Looser underwriting mix in the 2026-P1 ABS pool: WA APR fell to 10.67% while WA LTV rose to 97.89% and 75.2% of loans have original terms over 72 months; recent-months performance of the 2024 series has weakened

Governance/related-party risk: Fitch's governance score is 'deficient' (-1 notch); the Garcias control ~83% of voting rights and DriveTime (controlled by Ernest Garcia II) receives high-margin warranty commissions and payments for services/subleases; past title/registration suspensions in some states could recur and hurt the brand

Tariff/inflation pass-through risk: tariff-related new-car price hikes and inflation drove up reconditioning costs and retail depreciation, denting Q4 2025 profit (~8% share drop on Feb 19, 2026) and prompting J.P. Morgan, RBC and at least two other brokerages to cut price targets

Accounting-credibility overhang: short seller Gotham City Research alleged 2023-2024 earnings were overstated by more than $1 billion; Carvana rejected the allegations, but short interest remains elevated (~10.7% of free float as of Feb 17, 2026)

Guidance credibility/valuation risk: FY2026 EBITDA guidance midpoint ($2.85B) came in below consensus ($2.93B) even after a revenue beat, and the stock trades at ~32x forward earnings vs a ~46x 1-year average, with sell-side 12-month revenue growth expected to decelerate to 26.1%

Structural overhang: the share count on a full-conversion basis is 1.127 billion Class A shares (vs 721M basic), and the multi-class structure concentrates voting with the Garcia Parties - dilution and control risks persist

catalysts.claim: Q4 2026 earnings call: Carvana said that beginning with this call it will stop providing quarterly/annual outlooks and will shift primary reporting to GAAP metrics in 2027, making the Q4 print the last guided quarter
$600 million 5.500% senior unsecured notes due April 15, 2027 are the nearest bond maturity and come due within the next six months (rated BB-/RR4 by Fitch on 30-Jul-2026)
$1.5 billion floor plan facility matures in April 2027, requiring renewal within the next six months
Three ADESA full-buildout sites are under construction and all expected to begin production in 2027, supporting the capacity ramp toward 3 million units/year

event_driven.claim: Carvana announced successful upsize and pricing of a $1.66 billion senior secured Term Loan B facility (SOFR+225bps, 99.75 of par, 7-year), with proceeds plus cash to redeem in full its 9.00% Senior Secured Notes due 2030; transaction cuts cash interest ~$45M/year and is leverage-neutral

Short seller Gotham City Research alleged Carvana overstated its 2023-2024 earnings by more than $1 billion; the company rejected the allegations on Feb 18, 2026; short interest was elevated at ~14.84 million shares, ~10.7% of free float as of Feb 17, 2026
Carvana joined the S&P 500 index in December 2025, capping 2025 (no activist campaigns, spin-offs or buyback programs found in the corpus as of Nov 10, 2026)

Fitch notes free cash flow (~$700M/year expected from 2026) could fund growth initiatives including M&A, and the company has publicly stated deleveraging intentions and longer-term investment-grade aspirations

output.research_view: The thesis right now is the tension between hypergrowth and per-unit economics: Q3 2026 delivered Carvana's first 200,000+ unit quarter (217,385 units, +39%; revenue $8.04B, +42%; record $800M Adjusted EBITDA) and a $1.66B term-loan refinancing that cut cash interest ~$45M/year with net leverage at ~1.0x, yet GPU fell $365 YoY, Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to 10.0% from 11.3%, and the FY26 EBITDA guide (higher end of $2.7-3.0B) still undershot consensus. Watch the loan-sale engine - 56% of EBITDA depends on securitization markets that S&P shows loosening (WA APR 10.67%, LTV 97.9%) - plus the ~$45M/quarter GPU drift and fuel/logistics costs (~$200/unit Q3 hit) into the Q4 print, which will be the last quarter with formal guidance. Governance (Garcias' ~83% voting control, DriveTime related-party flows, Gotham City's >$1B overstatement allegations) and the $600M April 2027 unsecured maturity are the idiosyncratic overhangs an analyst should price before chasing the ~27% post-earnings rally.

credit_signals.claim: Fitch assigned Carvana a first-time Long-Term IDR of 'BB-' with Stable Outlook (Jul 30, 2026); senior secured notes rated 'BB+'/RR2 and unsecured notes 'BB-'/RR4

S&P carries Carvana Co. at BB-/Positive, and on Mar 4, 2026 published a presale for Carvana Auto Receivables Trust 2026-P1 (~$1.22B notes on a $1,050.7M pool of 39,517 loans), the first CRVNA series to include new-vehicle loans

Refinancing win: $1.66B term loan B priced Aug 12, 2026 at SOFR+225 (99.75 of face) to refinance the 9%-13% cash/PIK secured notes due 2030 ($1B set for redemption Aug 15, remainder Aug 22), cutting the rate ~3 points, saving ~$45M/year in cash interest and pushing maturities to Aug 15, 2033
Fitch withdrew the rating on the $659.9M 9% senior secured notes due Jun 1, 2030 as 'repaid' on Aug 24, 2026; nearest remaining bond maturity is the $600M 5.5% unsecured notes due Apr 15, 2027

As of June 30, 2026: total debt $5,236M, cash $2,630M, net debt $2,606M, net debt/TTM Adjusted EBITDA 1.0x (TTM Adjusted EBITDA $2,589M); debt composition: $3,929M senior secured notes, $107M senior unsecured notes, $485M real-estate financing, $396M securitization financing, $126M floor plan

Liquidity as of Sept 30, 2026: $5,120M committed liquidity resources and $7,503M total liquidity resources (up from $4.55B total liquidity as of Mar 31, 2026, which included $2.4B cash and $982M available on receivables-backed revolvers)

Leverage: EBITDAR leverage was 4.3x in 2024 and 2.4x in 2025; Fitch expects the low-2x range from 2026, and Q3 2026 carried a $53M loss on debt extinguishment from the early redemption of the secured notes due 2030

Loan origination/monetization generated ~$1.2B of profit in 2025 (56% of EBITDA), with ~$13B of 2025 originations monetized via Ally, ABS and fixed pool sales; a securitization freeze would create material liquidity needs; downgrade triggers include EBITDAR leverage sustained near 4x or fixed charge coverage ~2.5x

missing_fields: Exact Q4 2026 earnings report date (not yet announced; expected ~Feb 2027 based on prior-year timing)
Share repurchase/tender offer authorization (no program found in collected sources as of Nov 10, 2026)
Pending court docket/regulatory enforcement actions specific to Carvana in H2 2026 (only risk-factor references to FTC rulemaking and past state title/registration suspensions found)
Current-quarter analyst EPS consensus estimate (only revenue and EBITDA consensus found)

alternative_signals.claim: Capacity/channel: 21 ADESA locations now have integrated retail production (up from 16 integrated in 2025), with 3 full buildout sites under construction for 2027 production; annual reconditioning capacity ~1.5M units at full IRC utilization as of Dec 31, 2025

Recent commercial activity: same-day delivery expanded to Jacksonville (Oct 14, 2026), ADESA Orlando IRC integration (Oct 6, 2026), Phoenix Rising FC partnership extension into its 10th season (Oct 21, 2026)
Hiring: with ADESA site integrations Carvana has begun hiring local team members, with ~100 new jobs expected over time per IRC integration (e.g., ADESA Long Island, Oct 2025)

Market share: retail unit run-rate ~870,000/year (~2% of used market, ~1.5% overall) with ~40% growth while the industry was approximately flat - management credits broader selection, faster deliveries and lower customer loan rates

Pricing/financing: Carvana deliberately lowered customer-facing interest rates to drive growth, compressing other GPU (loan-sale gains -$307 in Q3 2026); it is also adding reconditioning capacity in Rio Linda, California, targeted at the one region where Q2 sales growth trailed

Cost watch item: management said big moves in gas prices and interest rates cost ~$200 per unit in Q3 2026; operations expense per retail unit rose $109 on higher fuel and logistics costs - flagged as the metric to watch in Q4

Street split: Needham retained a $100 price target and named Carvana a top pick, while Zacks assigned a #4 (Sell) rank after cutting its earnings estimate; Street consensus ~10 buys / 6 outperform / 7 holds / 1 sell with mean target ~$83 (Sept 2026)

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q3 2026 (quarter ended Sept 30, 2026): record 217,385 retail units sold (+39% YoY), revenue $8.040 billion (+42% YoY), net income $483 million (6.0% margin), record Adjusted EBITDA $800 million (10.0% margin), GAAP operating income $714 million (8.9% margin)

Q3 2026 beat consensus: revenue $8.04B vs S&P analyst consensus $7.67B (4.9% beat); Adjusted EBITDA $800M vs consensus $791.3M (1.1% beat); shares surged 8.4% to $63.99 immediately after the release and jumped 15.7% the next day
Full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.85 billion at the midpoint (higher end of $2.7-$3.0B) sits below analysts' consensus of $2.93 billion

Current guidance: for Q4 2026, a sequential increase in retail units sold, and full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA in the higher end of the previously communicated $2.7-$3.0 billion range, 'as long as the environment remains stable'
Q3 total gross profit per retail unit was $6,997, down $365 YoY (non-GAAP GPU $7,093, down $410); Adjusted EBITDA margin 10.0% vs 11.3% in Q3 2025

Prior quarter (Q2 2026): record 197,325 retail units (+38% YoY), revenue $7.376B (+52% YoY), net income $513M, Adjusted EBITDA $769M; company then guided FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $2.7-$3.0B (vs $2.24B in 2025)

Reporting change: beginning with the Q4 2026 earnings call Carvana does not plan to provide quarterly or annual outlooks, and will shift primary reporting to GAAP metrics in 2027; mid-term goal restated as 3 million retail units annually at 12.5% Operating margin between 2030-2035

insider_and_ownership.claim: Ernest C. Garcia II (Director, 10% owner), via wholly owned ECG II SPE II, LLC, sold 10,000,000 European-style covered call options on CVNA Class A shares on Oct 30, 2026 - $90.00 strike, $8.25 cash premium per option, expiring Nov 19, 2027 (Form 4 filed Nov 3, 2026); to secure the obligation he pledged 10,000,000 Class B shares and 12,500,000 Carvana Group Class A units; no Rule 10b5-1 plan reported

Schedule 13D/A Amendment No. 40 (event date Oct 30, 2026, filed Nov 3, 2026): Ernest C. Garcia II beneficially owns 212,211,585 Class A shares on an as-converted basis, or 22.7% of the class, based on 722,713,745 Class A shares outstanding as of Oct 26, 2026

CEO Ernest C. Garcia III Form 4 (filed Aug 4, 2026): 7,069 shares withheld at $62.36 for taxes on RSU vesting (code F) and 134,707 Class A shares acquired via RSUs at $0 on Aug 3, 2026, bringing direct holdings to 4,723,869 shares (plus 4.0M shares held indirectly via trusts)

Institutional buying (13Fs reported Aug 2026): CAS Investment Partners (Cliff Sosin) added 18.0M shares to 22.6M (~$1.48B); Viking Global added 9.5M to 12.3M; Lone Pine added 8.8M to 10.5M; Maverick Capital added 2.2M to 2.6M; Duquesne (Druckenmiller) initiated a new 151,000-share position
Recent CVNA insider filings on EDGAR: Form 144 filed Nov 9, 2026; Form 4 filed Nov 5, 2026; Form 144 filed Nov 4, 2026; Schedule 13D/A filed Nov 3, 2026; Form 4 filed Nov 3, 2026

Control: CEO Ernest Garcia III and his father Ernest Garcia II control ~83% of voting rights (10:1 Class B shares while the Garcia Parties hold at least 25% of Class A), with related-party transactions via DriveTime (Fitch governance assessed 'deficient', -1 notch)
